_meta.author: Emanuel Rechsteiner (original developer)
_meta.purpose: Complete onboarding and handoff reference for DocScraper. This document was prepared by the original developer to enable a senior developer to continue development without errors. It captures the full architecture, design decisions, known gotchas, and development history that would otherwise only exist in the original developer's head.
_meta.handoff_note: I (Emanuel Rechsteiner) built this project from scratch starting May 2025. This JSON contains everything I know about the codebase — the architecture decisions, the bugs I fixed, the gotchas that cost me hours, and the patterns I established. If something seems weird, check the 'known_issues_and_gotchas' section first. The ADRs in docs/decisions/ explain the WHY behind the big choices. Good luck, and feel free to reach out via the GitHub repo if you have questions.

project.name: DocScraper
project.description: Python toolkit for scraping documentation websites and post-processing them for optimal use in vector databases and LLM applications.

pipeline_stages.name: Scraping
pipeline_stages.description: Crawl documentation websites, convert HTML to clean markdown with YAML frontmatter metadata
pipeline_stages.output: Raw markdown files with YAML frontmatter (url, scraped_at, title) + _scrape_summary.json

pipeline_stages.name: Cleaning (Rule-based)
pipeline_stages.description: Remove navigation, boilerplate, headers/footers using regex pattern matching
pipeline_stages.output: Cleaned markdown files with reduced noise

pipeline_stages.name: Cleaning (LLM-enhanced)
pipeline_stages.description: Semantic content analysis using GPT-4o to identify main content vs navigation/boilerplate. Runs BEFORE rule-based cleaning on original content.
pipeline_stages.output: Semantically cleaned content with accurate boundary detection

pipeline_stages.name: Chunk Optimization
pipeline_stages.description: Split content into semantic chunks optimized for embedding models, respecting heading boundaries and code blocks
pipeline_stages.output: Chunked content with metadata (boundaries, token estimates)

pipeline_stages.name: Post-Processing (Full Pipeline)
pipeline_stages.description: Orchestrates cleaning + structuring + LLM classification + dependency graph + complexity scoring + topological sorting

design_principles: Graceful degradation: LLM features are optional, system falls back to rule-based
Checkpoint/resume: Long-running processes save checkpoints to prevent data loss
Dual interfaces: Every core feature has both CLI and GUI (Tkinter) interfaces
Dual scrapers: Advanced async (DocScraper) for production, simple sequential (SimpleDocScraper) for debugging
File-based storage: Markdown files + JSON metadata (no database required)
Optional imports: Try/except blocks for LLM dependencies
architecture.data_flow: Web Documentation → Scraper → Raw .md files → PostScraperCleaner (intelligent + rule-based) → Cleaned .md → DocPostProcessor (structure + classify + sort) → Vector DB Ready (chunks + index)

core.asyncio: Async I/O for scraping and post-processing

cleaning_pipeline_order: PASS 1: Intelligent content analysis (LLM, on ORIGINAL content for accurate line numbers)
PASS 2: Rule-based cleaning (regex patterns on LLM-cleaned content)
PASS 4: Chunk optimization (optional, for vector DB)
PostScraperCleaner.critical_design_decision: Intelligent analysis runs FIRST on original content to get accurate line numbers. Rule-based runs SECOND on the result.

prompt_strategy: Sends document with LINE NUMBERS (first 100 lines, middle 50 lines, last 50 lines)
LLM returns JSON with main_content_start/end and sections_to_remove/keep

IntelligentContentAnalyzer.fallback: If LLM fails, assumes main content is lines 20%-90% of document

known_issues_and_gotchas.description: LLM returns 1-indexed line numbers, Python uses 0-indexed arrays
Intelligent analysis MUST run on ORIGINAL content (not pre-cleaned) for accurate line numbers
known_issues_and_gotchas.impact: Running on cleaned content shifts line numbers and breaks boundary detection

known_issues_and_gotchas.description: Output directory is hardcoded to /Volumes/NvME-Satechi/VectorDatabase/ with timestamped subdirectories
known_issues_and_gotchas.impact: Won't work on other machines without changing this path

known_issues_and_gotchas.description: Patterns are compiled with re.MULTILINE | re.DOTALL. Invalid regex in a pattern raises ValueError at import time.
known_issues_and_gotchas.impact: A bad pattern prevents the entire module from loading

known_issues_and_gotchas.description: Uses urllib.request directly (not openai SDK) for API calls. DocPostProcessor.py uses AsyncOpenAI.
known_issues_and_gotchas.impact: Two different API call mechanisms in the same project — be aware when debugging

known_issues_and_gotchas.description: Remote development branch has src/ layout reorganization not present locally
known_issues_and_gotchas.action: Run 'git pull origin development' before starting new work

known_issues_and_gotchas.description: PostScraperCleaner uses try/except for llm_cleaner, intelligent_cleaner, chunk_optimizer imports
known_issues_and_gotchas.impact: If any of these modules have syntax errors, they silently fail to None and LLM features won't work

dependency_graph.description: Module import relationships (A → B means A imports from B)

code_conventions.type_hints: Full PEP 484 on all function signatures. Use Optional[] for nullable, List/Dict/Set from typing.
code_conventions.docstrings: Module-level docstrings, class docstrings, method docstrings. Descriptive style, not Google/NumPy format.
imports_order: 1. Standard library (asyncio, os, re, json, pathlib, dataclasses, typing, logging)
2. Third-party (crawl4ai, beautifulsoup4, openai, tenacity, networkx, sklearn, numpy)
code_conventions.error_handling: Try/except with logging.error() for API calls; raise ValueError for configuration validation; graceful fallbacks for optional features
code_conventions.logging: logging.getLogger(__name__) per module; logging.basicConfig() at module level; INFO level by default
code_conventions.data_structures: @dataclass with field(default_factory=list) for mutable defaults; __post_init__ for validation; to_dict() for serialization

steps: 1. Create new CleaningPattern instance in CLEANING_PATTERNS list
2. Assign appropriate PatternCategory (NAVIGATION, UI, BOILERPLATE, REDUNDANT)
3. Set confidence (0.0-1.0) — higher means more aggressive removal
4. Test regex pattern thoroughly — bad regex crashes at import time
5. DEFAULT_REGISTRY auto-includes all patterns in CLEANING_PATTERNS
